skills.summary: Randomly generate a one-week menu (7 days by default, with breakfast / lunch / dinner every day) from a self-contained dish library. Picks dishes at random, avoids repeating the same dish within the same meal slot across the week when the pool allows, prints a readable Markdown or plain-text menu, and is reproducible through a --seed flag. Implemented with the Python 3 standard library only; it does not call the Huawei Cloud CLI, any Huawei Cloud SDK, or any REST API, and it touches no cloud resource. Triggers include: "生成一周菜单", "随机生成菜单", "一周食谱", "规划一周饮食", "帮我排一周菜谱", "weekly menu", "random menu", "meal plan", "weekly meal planner".

skills.summary: Decode why a specific LinkedIn post performed unusually well. Breaks the post down into hook, structure, format, emotional triggers, timing, and audience match, then produces a reusable template the user can apply to their own content. Requires the Taplio MCP to pull live viral posts to study and fetch the user's own posts and analytics. Use when the user pastes a viral post they want to learn from.

latestVersion.changelog:
Initial release of the LinkedIn Viral Post Analyzer.

- Analyze LinkedIn posts across seven dimensions, from hook strength to format.
- Identify the post’s key performance levers and turn them into a reusable template.
- Use Taplio MCP data to ground analysis in the user’s profile, posts, and analytics.
- Require Taplio MCP; provide setup steps if it isn’t connected.

skills.summary: Surface the topics that are heating up right now in a given LinkedIn niche, with concrete angles the user can post about today. Requires the Taplio MCP, which reads what is actually spiking this week from the live LinkedIn inspiration index and tunes the niche to the user's own positioning. Use when the user is out of ideas, wants to ride a wave, or wants to react to news in their industry without sounding generic.

latestVersion.changelog:
Introduces a new LinkedIn trending topics scanner grounded in Taplio data.

- Uses the Taplio MCP to identify recent, high-engagement topics in the user’s niche.
- Suggests on-brand “with the wave” and contrarian angles, plus a post format for each topic.
- Requires Taplio MCP; if it’s unavailable, the skill stops and provides setup instructions.
- Notes that trend detection uses recent likes as an approximation, not real-time engagement velocity.

skills.summary: Help the user assemble a personal swipe file of high-performing LinkedIn posts, organized by hook pattern, format, and angle. The skill defines the structure, asks for inputs, turns saved posts into a usable reference library, then drafts the user's own post for every reference in the file (reusing structure, not substance) and saves the approved ones as drafts. It seeds the file with real high-performing posts from the live inspiration index and the user's own top performers. Use when the user wants to systematically learn from what works without copying it. Requires the Taplio MCP.

latestVersion.changelog:
Version 1.0.0 introduces a Taplio-powered workflow for building and using a LinkedIn swipe file.

- Organizes reference posts by hook pattern, format, angle, and why they were saved.
- Sources inspiration posts and the user’s top-performing posts through Taplio MCP.
- Creates an adaptable swipe-file structure, daily habit, and review prompts.
- Drafts an original post for every reference, reusing its structure—not its substance—and saves approved drafts to Taplio.
- Requires the Taplio MCP; the skill stops if it is unavailable.

skills.summary: Extract a publishable LinkedIn story from a raw user experience. The user dumps an experience (a project, a failure, a win, a meeting, a conversation), and the skill structures it into a story-arc post (situation, tension, turning point, lesson). Use when the user has lived something but does not know how to turn it into content. Requires the Taplio MCP to pull proven story angles from the user's niche and save the finished story as a draft.

latestVersion.changelog:

skills.summary: Write a LinkedIn comment that gets noticed by the post author and the audience, save it as a Taplio comment draft, and, only on the user's explicit go, schedule it to post under their name. Avoids the generic great-post trap : 3 options on one angle (add, disagree, story, framework, question), ranked by likelihood of being pinned or replied to, written after reading what the thread already says. Use after the user has a post in mind, a pick from the Comment Opportunity Finder, or a LinkedIn post url. Requires the Taplio MCP to read the post and its thread, save the draft, commit it, and confirm it went live.
